column1: # Declarations a unit repeats although a mirror in its own include graph
# already carries them (PORTING.md P-26; docs/status.md 3.75/3.76).  Written by
# `python3 tools/check-mirror-dupes.py --write-ratchet`.  A new hit fails the gate;
# deleting one is a two-step job per unit: drop the copy, `build-tu <unit>`, then

column4: glibc's `#define weak_alias(...)`; C's own spelling of the alias, not a duplicate of the mirror's

ftoastr.h 152-155: the unit's `usize` const is an array length, and a `macro_rules!` cannot be one in Rust - the mirror keeps C's macro and the unit needs the const, so both spellings are load-bearing

mktime.c 104-105's `#undef tzset / #define tzset() my_tzset ()`: C's own redirect
the generated `<time.h>` 841-842's `#define mktime rpl_mktime`: gnulib's redirect, C's own spelling
the generated `<time.h>` 1144-1145's `#define timegm rpl_timegm`: gnulib's redirect

bionic's `<unistd.h>` 299 declares `int pipe2 (int[2], int)` (measured in NDK 25.1-28.2) and android.c 369/1528 call it under the Android configuration, where no gnulib replacement applies; the mirror's `# define pipe2 rpl_pipe2` is the frozen Darwin substitution (`@REPLACE_PIPE2@` is 1 there) and android.c is outside the frozen build - two configurations' arms, not one declaration copied
lisp.h 5316's `# define emacs_fclose fclose`; the unit spells it with `#[link_name = "fclose"]`, a different namespace with the same effect - C's own redirect

the unit's copy is the `#[cfg (feature = "no_signbit")]` arm, i.e. C's `#ifndef signbit` dead text carried on purpose (P-51), while the mirror's is the live `<math.h>` macro - one C condition's two arms, not a duplicate

kept on purpose: the window.rs mirror spells the parameter `*mut c_void` (PORTING.md 0.1-2/P-72 rule 3) while this unit's call site passes `*mut buffer`; converging means window.rs including buffer.rs, which is that mirror owner's call

androidfns.c 1487's call sits in the `#ifndef ANDROID_STUBIFY` arm (C 1459-1489), and frame.h 1926 gates the declaration on `HAVE_WINDOW_SYSTEM` (frame.rs 1953) - which an Android arm carries without `have_android`: the unit keeps C's own copy under the complement `not (feature = "have_window_system")` gate, the `Display_Info` copy at androidfns.rs 417 class, so the two copies never coexist
